proposed_method: Factor (Bq/t coal) = mass concentration (Bq/kg) x 1000, by country/basin; head activities for U238+, Th230, Ra226+, Pb210+, Po210, Th232, Ra228+, K40, assuming Pb-210 and Po-210 in equilibrium with Ra-226 in the unburned coal (flag). Typical 20 Bq/kg U-238 and Th-232, 50 Bq/kg K-40; country ranges from S0001 Table 25; US basin values from COALQUAL (S0201) and S0216; China U 2.43 mg/kg (about 30 Bq/kg) from S0220.
notes: No pre-1950 measurements; but pre-1950 production was about 40% US, 31% UK, 12% Germany (S0230 country sums), whose coals have been measured. Apply production-weighted modern country values with wide bounds.

proposed_method: Liberated Rn222+ via mine ventilation (release route ventilation). Factor = Bq per t coal; China measured 9.3e5 Bq/t typical (1.9e5 large, 1.3e6 medium, 3.5e6 small mines). Waste-rock radon is not in UNSCEAR.
notes: No measurements; poorer ventilation (small and private mines) argues for the high end. UNSCEAR 1993 world release 30-800 TBq/a.

proposed_method: Liberated mine drainage (route mine_drainage). Poland measured: Ra-226 release 400 MBq/d (1987), 219 (1995), 120 (2003), 77 (2006) and Ra-228 380, 258, 170 MBq/d (1995, 2003, 2006). Express per t coal using Polish hard-coal output (about 190 Mt in 1987, see S0230) as a first factor (order 0.8 kBq Ra-226 per t in 1987, falling to a quarter by 2006: modelled, to be recomputed) and apply only to coalfields with Ra-bearing brines (type A/B); elsewhere use a low-end bound near zero. Germany (Ruhr) and UK exist but unread (S0250).
notes: Radium-bearing waters were noticed in Polish mines in the early 1960s and routinely monitored from the 1970s, but no flow-weighted release before 1987 was found. Model Upper Silesia from coal output x the 1987 factor as an upper bound.

proposed_method: Residue coal_mine_water_sludge (Impounded; underground deposits partly Re-isolated). Activity = retained fraction of mine-water radium (retained fraction conflicting: more than 70% in S0222, about 40% in S0225, about 66% from the S0222 1995 table) x radium inflow. Activity concentrations: underground BaSO4 deposits to 400,000 Bq/kg, pond sediments median 409 and mean 706 Bq/kg Ra-226 (n=39), about 5 million m3 in 25 working Polish ponds.
notes: No inventory before the late 1980s.
